title: Independently certify all-length receiver-window floors with two exact algorithms
body:
The bounded searches in #4546/#4567 leave an all-length gap. This adds a proof and source-bound certificate that **no finite shear word improves the transport invoice in any of the 128 adjacent #4470 receiver windows**, with the same three persistent fields, monotone frames and fixed entrance/exit frames. There is no word-length or rational-coefficient cap. The conclusion holds for every nonnegative concave rank price with f(0)=0, including r^(1-C) for every 0<C<1. No new κ or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

- The finite-state relaxation tracks dimensions, chronological source dependence and paid gaps: **1,496 states, 4,730 transitions and 239 terminal profiles across 128 windows**. The written containment/termination argument explains why closure covers arbitrary length, including zero-cost cycles.
- Exact truncated-rank sums prove the concave-cost order. A separate Dijkstra implementation, with no paid-profile history, corroborates **all 248 integer cost minima**. The incumbent attains each floor.
- Controls cover 894 actual geometric prefixes, 22,621 exact directed coefficient prefixes, a genuine cheaper-path fixture and chronology/terminal-charge/cost-order failures.
- All seven constructor inputs are authenticated by Git blob and SHA256. The complete per-window receipt reproduces field-for-field, including JSON types. Neither predecessor's acceptance code is imported.

## Scope and coordination

Started from canonical main `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`; fetched it again before submission and it was unchanged. Priority revision 7 and selected κ = 23/10000 are untouched. Pushed head: `23c515a3c071a6bfdd1fe80bc67cea55f6d43643`. The diff only adds `research/receiver-window-all-length-floor/`.

The initial overlap snapshot paginated 355 open PRs / 3,470 Discussion records. The refresh (355 / 3,486) exposed concurrent #4573, #4574 and #4577, which are credited. **This is independent corroboration and a separately reviewable certificate, with no exclusive novelty or priority claim.** The implementation was developed before reading those claims. #4577 reports a stricter directed graph with 1,303 states; this package's more permissive bidirectional relaxation reaches the same 239 profiles and adds a separate shortest-path check. No concurrent package is imported or certified here.

[Canonical Discussion #4572](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4572) and [handoff pointer](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19117827). #4567's newer head `5ac594d1bc1e6d91f20ef8157f38bb9b29768bfd` adds nonadjacent/single-contact checks but still labels its all-length explanation unproved. Local-note overlap coverage is sparse and explicitly incomplete.

## Validation

Windows, CPython 3.12.0, standard library only:

```text
python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/receiver-window-all-length-floor --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS
python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/receiver-window-all-length-floor
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result
python -I -O -B research/receiver-window-all-length-floor/verify.py --self-test
  all controls pass
python -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/receiver-window-all-length-floor
  PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES (23c515a..., 14 package/input files)
```

The generic selected baseline was attempted but cannot inspect selected package roots omitted in this sparse checkout; no selected-baseline or cold-replay success is claimed.

## Limitations and credit

The result excludes only the fixed three-field monotone-frame transport model. Extra/owned fields, decreasing frames/resets, changed boundaries/warps, joint or larger windows and full native/physical/precision/compiler admission remain outside scope. Overlapping-window conclusions cannot be added. The README and TASK give bounded next questions for a fully charged fourth-field contract or a joint window with a movable internal boundary.

Credit Chris R / Clear1nsight (#4546/#4543), Ryanson Jonathan (#4567), Cinna Davis (#4470), zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and the retained scalar/Clifford/geometry/outer contributors, plus the concurrent investigations above. Prepared by Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. This is author-checked evidence, not independent human or formal-kernel verification.
